extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of philosophy (particularly epistemology/transcendental philosophy); philosophers developing systematic metaphysical theories
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and theses for constructing a transcendental (subject-centered) philosophical system: how to choose postulates, the methodological duties of starting from subject or object, and the identification of self-consciousness as the ultimate principle of knowledge. Includes ten numbered theses defining criteria for truth, being, and the role of self-consciousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of postulates in philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce postulates in philosophy analogously to mathematics: primary constructions (intuitions) are postulated rather than demonstrated, serving as the starting points of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: geometry begins with the point in motion or the line; philosophy must similarly postulate the most original construction for the inner sense. The mathematician begins with an intuition (practical idea) rather than a demonstrable proposition; philosophy should emulate this by adopting primary intuitions for inner experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceed from the most original construction for the inner sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy, to achieve evidence, must begin from the most original productive act or construction of the inner sense (an intuition) rather than deriving it from outward objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike geometry, the inner sense cannot be directed by external images; its direction is largely determined by an act of freedom. The inward construction is the necessary starting point for arriving at philosophical evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophic capacity test: Know thyself
rubrics_metrics.description: The postulate and test of philosophic capacity is 'Know thyself' — self-knowledge (self-consciousness) is the foundational intuition for philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophy is both practical and speculative; all knowledge rests on the coincidence of object and subject. The immediate self-consciousness is the fixed point to which all knowledge is mortised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sectarianism; reconcile diverse systems
rubrics_metrics.description: A true philosophical system should explain and collect fragments of truth scattered across apparently incongruous systems, avoiding sectarian exclusion of others' conceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical doctrines (e.g., sceptics, Pythagoreans, Platonists, Aristotelians, Stoics) each contain partial truths that a sound system will unite in a central perspective showing regularity and coincidence of parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish two methodological starts: objective-first vs subjective-first
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two equally possible methodological cases: (1) take the objective (nature) first and explain how the subjective (intelligence) supervenes; or (2) take the subjective (self-consciousness) first and explain how an objective coincident arises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If objective is first, the problem is to account for the supervention of subjectivity (natural philosophy's task). If subjective is first, the problem is to account for the emergence of objective reality (transcendental philosophy's task). Either approach must be pursued with strict adherence to its own principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological purification by scientific scepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcendental/intelligential philosophy must purify the mind by a voluntary, scientific scepticism that excludes unconscious prejudices and assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is distinct from vain scepticism; it targets original innate prejudices (e.g., the presumption that things exist without us) and serves to attain future certainty (Descartes' meditations offered as example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict separation of principles between sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Success in any science depends on austere adherence to its own principles and careful exclusion of those belonging to the opposite pole (objective vs subjective sciences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural philosophers must avoid introducing subjective suppositions (occult qualities, final causes) and transcendental philosophers must avoid importing objective explanatory assumptions (impressions/configurations in the brain as primitives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis I: Truth correlates with being
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth is correlative to being: knowledge without a correspondent reality is no knowledge; to know is an active verb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that knowledge presupposes something known; knowledge is not passive representation but an active relation to reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis II: Distinction between mediate and immediate truth
rubrics_metrics.description: All truth is either mediate (derived from other truths) or immediate and original (absolute, self-grounded). Mediate truths have conditional certainty (formula B.A.), immediate truths are absolute (formula A.A.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A chain of truths without a first principle is inadequate; seek an absolute starting truth to avoid infinite regress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis III: Requirement of an absolute self-grounded truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy must seek an absolute truth capable of communicating certainty to other positions — a self-grounded, unconditional truth that is known by its own light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle must be self-predicative and exclude the need for a cause or antecedent; it should supply certainty to other positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis IV: Uniqueness of the absolute principle
rubrics_metrics.description: There can be only one such absolute principle; multiplicity would require each to refer to another and so negate self-establishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness can be shown a priori (by reasoning about the impossibility of multiple self-establishing principles) and a posteriori when the principle is discovered and shows universal antecedence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis V: The absolute principle is neither a mere thing nor a mere subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The absolute cannot be any 'thing' (object) because every thing implies other things; neither can it be a subject exclusively; it must be the identity of subject and object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments: an infinite independent thing is contradictory; objects presuppose subjects. Since no third is conceivable, the principle must be that which is both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis VI: The absolute principle manifests as I AM (self-consciousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle reveals itself in the sum or I AM (spirit, self, self-consciousness) where object and subject, being and knowing, are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The spirit is a perpetual self-duplication into object and subject; it becomes subject by constructing itself objectively to itself and is only an object for itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis VII: Spirit as act; self-consciousness implies will and freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-knowledge occurs only through self; the spirit must be an act (self-representation), hence intelligence/self-consciousness is impossible except by and in a will; freedom must be assumed as a ground of philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since the spirit dissolves identity to be conscious (fit alter et idem), self-consciousness presupposes volition; thus freedom is a necessary presupposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis VIII: Objective origin implies finitude; spirit reconciles finitude and infinity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever is originally objective is necessarily finite; the spirit, not originally an object, cannot be conceived as exclusively finite or infinite but as the union/reconciliation of both — the process of production and life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existence and recurrence of this contradiction (finite/infinite) constitutes the dynamic process of life and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis IX: Role of the will as mediate principle; primacy of self-consciousness in transcendental philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: The common principle (principium commune essendi et cognoscendi) subsists in a will and is the mediate principle of every science but the immediate principle of transcendental philosophy; transcendental philosophy confines itself to the subjective pole; self-consciousness is the highest principle of knowing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All theses here refer to the subjective pole (scientia scientiae). The aim is an absolute principium cognoscendi (principle of knowing) found in the act of self-duplication/self-consciousness, not an absolute principium essendi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis X: The transcendental philosopher seeks the last element within knowing itself
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcendental philosophy inquires into the last in our knowing beyond which we cannot pass; the act of self-consciousness is asserted as the source and principle of all possible knowledge for us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even assuming the objective first, one cannot pass beyond the principle of self-consciousness without infinite regress or arbitrary stopping; thus natural and transcendental philosophy converge on an absolute identity of subject and object (absolute as self-conscious will/intelligence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological admonition: assume self-consciousness as ground to avoid infinite regress
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid an infinite regress of grounds, philosophy must either break the series arbitrarily or posit an absolute identity (self-consciousness) as the terminus; positing self-consciousness prevents the regress and provides unity/system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This legitimizes beginning with 'I KNOW MYSELF' to end with 'I AM', proceeding from the self to an absolute that reconciles philosophy and religion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical implication for natural philosophy: tendency toward spiritualization of laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural science, though beginning with material phenomena, unconsciously tends toward spiritualizing laws into laws of intuition and intellect; ultimate natural philosophy places reality in an absolute identical with intelligence/self-consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As theorizing advances, phenomena's material husk drops away leaving formal laws; examples include optical phenomena as geometry, magnetism losing trace of matter, and some Newtonians treating gravitation as immediate spiritual influence.
